name: Zircon-Tide
description: Zircon-Tide orbits a binary star system, and its warm ocean reflects the paired suns in shimmering bands of white and pale gold that earned the planet its crystalline name. Shallow seas stretch across most of the surface, rarely exceeding two hundred meters in depth, with chains of volcanic islands providing the only dry land. The twin sunsets paint the water in impossible colors, zircon-clear whites giving way to deep amber and violet.

The warm, breathable air is thick with moisture and the briny tang of a living ocean. Schools of translucent fauna drift just below the surface, visible as moving shadows against the bright seafloor. The shallow waters amplify sound, and the calls of larger marine creatures echo across kilometers, creating a constant natural chorus that rises and falls with the tidal cycles of the binary suns.

A colonial settlement called Tidebreak was established on the largest island chain forty years ago, initially thriving on aquaculture and marine research. Industrial runoff and aggressive harvesting practices disrupted the thermal vent ecosystems, triggering a decline in the native fauna that has accelerated over the past decade. The colonists recognize the damage but face economic pressures that make remediation difficult.

Zircon-Tide's fauna includes species with unique pharmaceutical properties, but the very harvesting that makes them valuable threatens their survival. Conservation groups and corporate interests clash openly in Tidebreak's town council, and the colonial charter is up for renewal. The binary system's tidal forces are slowly increasing volcanic activity on the islands, adding geological urgency to an already fraught situation.
